diagnosis.reason: Widening the AR window from p=16 to p=32 decreased target point-wise F1 from 0.7200 to 0.6897 (delta -0.0303), with all other pipeline dimensions frozen (diff_order=1, min-max, batch_size=128, epochs=100, lr=0.001). The hypothesis that the curve's high lag-1 autocorrelation (0.998) implies longer-range dependence exploitable by a wider AR window is refuted on the target metric: the differenced series' predictive structure is better captured by the shorter p=16.

research_decision.hypothesis: Baseline chosen: component/AR/naive/TODS/234 is the mandated initial baseline and current global best (point-wise-f1 0.72). Candidate rationale: curve 234 has lag-1 autocorrelation 0.998 (slowly decaying temporal dependence), so the incumbent AR window p=16 likely truncates exploitable structure; widening the AR window to p=32 while keeping diff_order=1/min-max (all else frozen) is a new untested pipeline that should capture longer-range dependence and improve point-wise F1.
research_decision.next_action_rationale: The refutation is directionally informative: p=32 degraded the target metric, so the incumbent's advantage likely lies on the short-window side of p=16. p=8 is the untested opposite probe to test whether shrinking below the default further improves point-wise F1; if it also degrades, the window dimension is exhausted and preprocessing (z-score vs min-max on the skewed curve) becomes the next dimension to explore.
